gotchas.text: TLSF allocator in tlsf.hpp uses its own malloc/free — alignment guarantee is implementation-specific, likely 16-byte. Use unaligned SIMD load/store (_mm256_loadu_si128) not aligned variants.
Newton fraction blowup: root(2, iter) doubles bits each iteration. Benchmarks use iter=10 which is safe. SIMD does not affect this.
Header-only globals (nn_izero etc.) cause multi-TU linker errors. main.cpp is single TU — safe. SIMD targets are also single TU compilations of the same main.cpp with different flags.
normalize(3) semantics: bit1=trim trailing zero bits (trivial for SIMD since trailing zeros from add/sub are data-dependent, not SIMD-induced)
The commented-out SSE2 multiplication in ii.hpp used 32-bit words (__m128i _mm_mul_epu32). Our AVX/AVX2 add/sub uses 64-bit words (_mm256_add_epi64) — different intrinsics, same file shares both.
immintrin.h is already included unconditionally in tlsf.hpp line 49 — no need for platform or macro guards around the #include. The functions themselves must be guarded by NN_HAVE_AVX2 / NN_HAVE_AVX.

prior_decisions.decision: Multi-variant baseline JSON format: nested {variant: {benchmark_name: nanos}}
rationale: Supports adding new variants (avx, avx2) without schema change

prior_decisions.decision: NUMERIC_THREADS env var for runtime single-thread forcing
Unaligned SIMD load/store to handle TLSF allocation
rationale: No alignment contract from TLSF allocator
Near-zero performance cost on Haswell+ for 128/256-bit unaligned loads

prior_decisions.decision: No runtime CPU dispatch — compile-time selection via -DNN_HAVE_AVX2
rationale: Each benchmark binary targets a specific ISA level
CPU feature detection would add complexity without benefit for controlled benchmarking

prior_decisions.decision: Only SIMD-accelerate Phase 1 overlap loop — leave Phases 2 and 3 scalar
rationale: Phase 1 is the hot loop (processes min(length_a, length_b) words)
Phase 2 runs at most the difference between lengths (typically small)
Phase 3 is 1-2 iterations — overhead of SIMD setup not justified
Scalar remainder for < vector-width count avoids partial-vector complexity

prior_decisions.decision: Use addp/addm/addz dispatch as-is — no SIMD in the dispatch functions
rationale: SIMD is inside each specialized function, not in the dispatcher
